study type: Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional study
cohort: 314,623 women who delivered in 359 health facilities in 29 countries in Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East
finding: This analysis of a multicountry database supports the concept of obstetric transition, finding that maternal health indicators and interventions vary significantly across different stages of this transition.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery and labor induction rates were 2.4 and 2.6 times higher, respectively, in countries at Stage IV of obstetric transition compared to those at Stage II.
